biography: José Augusto Jr., a name synonymous with raw aggression and relentless pursuit in the Brazilian Copa Fusca scene, hails from the vibrant favelas of Rio de Janeiro. His racing journey began, not on the asphalt, but on the dirt tracks, tearing through makeshift circuits in go-karts cobbled together from discarded parts. It was here, amidst the dust and the cheers of his community, that his innate talent for speed and fearless overtaking blossomed. A chance encounter with a local mechanic, impressed by José's audacious maneuvers, led to his first opportunity in a Copa Fusca team. His debut season was a baptism by fire, filled with daring overtakes and occasional crashes, quickly earning him a reputation as a driver who leaves it all on the track. Now, at 37, José is at his peak, a seasoned veteran still hungry for victories, battling younger rivals while carrying the hopes of his community with every race.
drivingStyle: José's driving style is best described as controlled chaos. He's an aggressive late-braker, often diving into corners with a seemingly reckless abandon that leaves rivals scrambling. Tire management isn't his forte; he pushes from the start, relying on his raw speed and car control to compensate. Under pressure, José thrives, transforming into an even more formidable opponent. Some call him reckless, but his fans admire his unwavering commitment to pushing the limits.

careerHighlight: Winning the Copa Fusca championship in 2018 after a season-long battle with Ricardo Silva, securing the title in the final race with a breathtaking last-lap overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2020 championship decider due to a mechanical failure, ending his title hopes in devastating fashion.
